tier_reason: Upgraded B to A: every Codon and PyPy3 number in the record matches the Codon and 'Python3 PYPY' rows of kostya/jit-benchmarks README.md, and the suite is fully reproducible. The benchmark code is public (<bench>/test.codon.py vs <bench>/test.py, build and run commands in tools/languages.rb: 'codon build --release'; docker/codon, docker/pypy3), versions are stated (Codon 0.15.5, PyPy 7.3.11 official binaries, CPython 3.10.7), and the CPU is stated (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Codon 0.15.5 installed by exaloop's install.sh in docker/codon, built with 'codon build --release' (kostya/jit-benchmarks tools/languages.rb); PyPy 7.3.11 official linux64 binary (python 3.9.16, gcc 10.2.1); CPython 3.10.7 from Ubuntu 22.10; C rows gcc 12.2.0. Times are measured inside each program (time() marks written to stderr), so Codon's 4-6 s compile time is reported separately.
corrections.claimed_speedup: kostya/jit-benchmarks best times in s, Codon vs PyPy3: brainfuck 2.05 vs 8.77; brainfuck2 1.91 vs 11.03; binarytrees 1.0 vs 3.84; fasta 1.66 vs 3.19; knucleotide 2.69 vs 3.7 (1 run each); matmul 0.25 vs 0.36; nbody 2.23 vs 4.44; spectralnorm 0.53 vs 0.71. Slower on fannkuchredux 1.82 vs 0.71 and mandelbrot 0.65 vs 0.54; failed on pidigits, regexdna and revcomp. Same page, Codon vs CPython 3.10.7: binarytrees 1.0 vs 73.15, brainfuck2 1.91 vs 142.26, mandelbrot 0.65 vs 37.52, matmul 0.25 vs 22.73, nbody 2.23 vs 53.72, spectralnorm 0.53 vs 20.69, fannkuchredux 1.82 vs 4.04 (about 2x to 90x, derived from page data). README: typical speedups over vanilla Python on the order of 10-100x or more, on a single thread.
corrections.caveats: Codon compiles a statically typed Python subset ahead of time with LLVM; it is not a drop-in Python runtime. The suite ran Codon on separate test.codon.py sources adapted for Codon (typed class fields such as Optional[TreeNode], a restructured binarytrees create function, copy.copy in place of copy.deepcopy in nbody), while PyPy and CPython ran test.py. Independent shootout is a 2023 snapshot with Codon 0.15.5; the Codon rows were added in the 2023-03-30 'Add codon' commit, after the round-1 date (2023-02-28) in the header. Codon failed to run pidigits, regexdna and revcomp and lost to PyPy on fannkuchredux and mandelbrot. Best-time column excludes the 4-6 s compile time; knucleotide and some PyPy rows are a single run. Benchmarks are simple single-thread kernels. exaloop.io benchmarks page and the Codon paper (CC 2023) were not opened (blocked). The repository is Apache-2.0 today (LICENSE checked); Codon 0.15.5, the version benchmarked, was released under BSL-1.1, so check the license of the version you use.

notes: All record numbers verified row by row on the kostya/jit-benchmarks README; upgraded to A because code, versions, build flags (codon build --release) and CPU are public. Main shortcomings: Codon ran adapted typed sources rather than the same test.py, it is an AOT compiler for a Python subset, and it lost to PyPy on 2 of 10 kernels and failed 3 others.

tier_reason: The README states 34.6% faster than LuaJIT's interpreter and 185% faster than PUC Lua 5.1 (i7-12700H). The benchmark code is public (luabench/, run_bench.sh) and the build flags are public, but run_bench.sh only runs luajitr, and the baseline builds (LuaJIT and PUC Lua with GC disabled) are not scripted or specified, so it is not A. B rests on the peer-reviewed OOPSLA 2026 Deegen paper (doi 10.1145/3798246), whose abstract (WebSearch snippet only; arXiv, ACM, Stanford and author pages blocked) reports 1.31x over LuaJIT's interpreter across 44 benchmarks. On README evidence alone it would be C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Current build: Clang/LLVM 19.1.6 patched and built from source in the repo's docker image (dockerfile/build_docker_image.sh), RELEASE flavor '-DNDEBUG -O3 -fno-pic -fno-pie -mbmi -msse4 -mfsgsbase' (CMakeLists.txt), built via 'python3 ljr-build make release'. run_bench.sh pins to CPU core 4 with taskset and wall-clock-times each benchmark with bash time, sleeping 3 s between runs. The toolchain behind the README numbers and the builds and flags of the LuaJIT and PUC Lua baselines (GC disabled) are not stated.
corrections.workload: 44 Lua benchmarks in luabench/ (list in run_bench.sh; k-nucleotide and revcomp read a 5,000,000-line FASTA input). The README footnote says 5 repetitions with a geometric mean; the current run_bench.sh runs each benchmark 7 times. Interpreter vs LuaJIT's interpreter (JIT off) and vs PUC Lua 5.1, GC disabled in all implementations.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README: interpreter is 34.6% faster than LuaJIT's interpreter and 185% faster than the official PUC Lua 5.1 interpreter (geometric average over all benchmarks). OOPSLA 2026 paper abstract (WebSearch snippet only): over 44 benchmarks the interpreter is 2.79x faster than PUC Lua and 1.31x faster than LuaJIT's interpreter; the baseline JIT is 4.60x faster than PUC Lua but on average 33% slower than LuaJIT's optimizing JIT (faster on 13 of 44).

notes: README claim and footnote verified; the paper numbers come only from search snippets of the abstract (dl.acm.org and arXiv listings), not from the paper body. Shortcomings: it beats LuaJIT's interpreter but not LuaJIT's tracing JIT (its baseline JIT is 33% slower on average); no GC, so baselines were also run with GC off; x86-64 Linux only; work in progress, last commit 2025-02-18; baseline LuaJIT version not stated in the README (the record's '2.1' is unverified); the bench script does not run the baselines.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: PHP 8.2.3 built from source in docker/php8 ('./configure --prefix /opt/php8 --with-gmp', configure default CFLAGS) with the Ubuntu 22.10 base image's gcc (12.2.0 per the versions table). JIT row: 'php -dmemory_limit=512M -dzend_extension=opcache.so -dopcache.enable_cli=1 -dopcache.enable=1 -dopcache.jit_buffer_size=500M -dopcache.jit=1255' (tracing JIT); baseline row: 'php -dmemory_limit=512M' with no opcache loaded (kostya/jit-benchmarks tools/languages.rb).
corrections.claimed_speedup: kostya/jit-benchmarks best times in s, PHP JIT vs PHP: mandelbrot 0.58 vs 5.51; fannkuchredux 0.77 vs 2.54; nbody 7.0 vs 21.77; spectralnorm 2.51 vs 6.48; binarytrees 2.93 vs 5.84; fasta 2.46 vs 4.64; knucleotide 1.96 vs 2.87 (1 run); revcomp 2.06 vs 2.27 (1 run); roughly equal on regexdna (1.39 vs 1.4) and pidigits (1.57 vs 1.71).
corrections.caveats: Compares the JIT with PHP's own interpreter, which is not one of the category baselines (PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot). The baseline row runs without opcache loaded at all, so the gain mixes the opcache optimizer with the JIT. Cross-language rows on the same page (different programs per language): PHP JIT is slower than PyPy3 on fannkuchredux (0.77 vs 0.71), mandelbrot (0.58 vs 0.54), nbody (7.0 vs 4.44) and spectralnorm (2.51 vs 0.71), and slower than LuaJIT on fannkuchredux, fasta, knucleotide, mandelbrot, nbody and spectralnorm; Node is faster on most kernels. This is an independent 2023 snapshot of simple benchmarks-game kernels; the README header says PHP8.1 but the versions table says 8.2.3. php-src master is BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE checked); released versions before the relicense, including the 8.2.3 tested, carry the PHP License 3.01. I did not open the php-src JIT sources or the PHP RFC.

notes: All numbers verified; blank rows confirmed as no-opcache runs from tools/languages.rb, and upgraded to A because the build, JIT flags, code and CPU are public. Shortcomings: off-baseline (PHP interpreter, not PyPy/LuaJIT/V8/HotSpot), behind LuaJIT and PyPy on numeric kernels, and opcache and JIT gains are not separated.
